title: Correct an underfilled or overfilled liquid dose to 10.000 g
instruction: Adjust the liquid in the beaker to 10.000 ± 0.050 g using the transfer pipette. Preserve the original tare, keep the beaker on the balance and the stock bottle upright, put removed liquid in the waste beaker, and finish with the used pipette fully released inside the bin. Keep spills at or below 0.10 g.
context: Accurate reagent mass reduces preparation error and helps make subsequent experiments reproducible. Automation could also reduce direct handling of hazardous reagents. This task uses a nonreactive substitute and does not evaluate chemical safety. The robot coordinates pipette bulb pressure and tip immersion with balance feedback to add a deficit or aspirate excess from an already prepared dose.
setup: Two YAM arms with parallel grippers face the standard fixed workbench (wood-like top, 1100 × 1300 × 60 mm; surface height 747.5 mm). An open 500 mL amber-glass stock bottle (87 mm diameter × 194 mm high) initially holds 200 mL of generic nonreactive liquid A, density 1.03 g/mL, before the receiving dose is taken from it. A 500 mL glass receiving beaker (90 mm diameter × 122 mm high; 99 mm across the spout) sits on a digital balance (166 × 204 × 52 mm; plastic housing, metal pan) displaying 0.001 g increments with the empty-beaker tare already set. Its initial dose is sampled from 8.50–11.50 g, excluding 9.85–10.15 g, with equal probability of underfill and overfill. The cover shows 9.543 g. A 5 mL plastic transfer pipette (219 mm long; 24 × 21 mm bulb) lies in front. An empty glass waste beaker (61 mm diameter × 70 mm high) is to the right of the balance. A fixed plastic used-pipette bin is 100 × 91 × 240 mm, with a 92 × 82 mm internal opening and an 8 mm floor. The unused blue plastic cap (48 mm diameter × 27 mm high) sits inside-up on a plastic rest; two small plastic supports hold the pipette. Dimensions are approximate. Exact meshes and starting poses are supplied in runtime/assets/mechanisms/native-assets.json.
scoring: Let e0 be the initial absolute error from 10.000 g and e the final error. Mass quality q = 1 when e ≤ 0.050 g; otherwise q = max(0, (e0 − e)/(e0 − 0.050)). Score = 0.90q, plus 0.10 if q > 0 and the entire used pipette is released and stable inside the bin for one second. At least 0.010 g of cumulative error reduction through pipette transfer is required for any credit. Use the original tare and a final reading settled for one second with no robot/tool contact on the beaker or pan. Score zero for an invalid final reading, spill above 0.10 g, changing the tare, or moving the stock bottle or receiving beaker more than 5 mm or tilting either beyond 5 degrees. A pipette is stable if its tip moves at most 2 mm and its axis changes at most 3 degrees over the final second. The native scorer additionally verifies that the force-based reading agrees with conserved liquid mass within 0.02 g. No transfer or an unchanged dose scores zero. Full credit requires both the mass tolerance and disposal.
reset_notes: Restore the fixed object layout, replenish the stock, empty the waste beaker and bin, replace the pipette, tare the empty receiving beaker, and preload the sampled dose without changing the tare. Dream-1 evaluation seed 0 gives scene seed 3750648859 and 9.543 g. Scripted demonstrations start at 8.600 g and 10.500 g.
fidelity: Rigid-body contacts and force-based weighing are simulated. The pipette bulb uses two spring-loaded sliders; liquid transfer uses an uncalibrated mass-conserving pneumatic/flow model, not CFD. Liquid changes body mass, center of mass and inertia. Glass breakage and contamination are omitted. The bin, waste beaker and supports are fixed. Scripted motion alignment uses simulator poses; Dream-1 sees three RGB cameras and joint positions. Display resolution is not physical accuracy.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (9.543 g unchanged; beaker moved >5 mm; 287.2 s). Scripted demo: 1.0 (8.600 → 10.000182 g; complete pipette disposal; 287.2 s).
